description: Trigger evals for skill-vet: it fires when a third-party agent skill or plugin sits in a local folder and has not been installed yet, while mcp-server-vet, security-review, review-hard and capture-references handle MCP servers, security review of our own code, general risk review, and saving web references.

should_trigger: I downloaded a skill pack from a random repo into ~/quarantine/seo-helper. Can you check it is safe before I install it?
is this claude plugin from the marketplace ok to add? want a verdict first
Read every file in this candidate skill folder, including the scripts and tests, not only SKILL.md. I need to know if it phones home, touches my dotfiles or edits CLAUDE.md.
A teammate sent a plugin with a SKILL.md and a setup.sh. Look for hidden unicode, shell execution and credential access, then tell me install, decline or sandbox.
Its description says it only formats markdown, but the folder has a 300 line python file. Does the code match what it claims?

should_not_trigger.prompt: A third-party MCP server exposes filesystem tools and I want to add it to my config. Inspect its tools and scopes first.
This slice encrypts stored bank account numbers and adds a CSV export of customer PII. Check the crypto choices and what data the export could leak before we ship.
Review the diff of the skill we wrote ourselves in this repo for correctness and maintainability risks.
Someone posted a skill on a blog. Fetch the page, summarize it and keep it in the project references.
Three marketplace skills claim to help with code review. Compare them from their public docs and tell me which fits our workflow best.
